# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly, over fifty  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c19 P5](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Jamesina  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c6 P12](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0012)</sub>; Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly triangular, pink-cheeked face and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope. She has snow-white hair worn in quaint, old-fashioned puffs over her ears. She dresses in a fashionably old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is a sweet, jovial, and cheerful woman with an unquenchable, youthful spirit. Although she holds traditional, old-fashioned opinions and believes in doing one's duty, she is deeply tolerant, candid, and loves a good joke. She possesses a dry wit, does not hesitate to speak her mind, and displays a warm, motherly affection toward those in her care. She also loves cats and is indulgent toward her own preferences.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059), [v3 c16 P63](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0063), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c37 P11](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0011), [v3 c37 P26](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0026)_

- Old-fashioned in her ways and opinions  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

- Skillful at knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep a comfortable home for her student charges at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000)</sub>
- To ensure her cats are well cared for  <sub>[v3 c16 P69](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0069), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina lived alone in a large house after her only daughter, Elizabeth, married and left for a foreign mission field in India. Being lonely, she accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport and act as housekeeper and chaperone for her niece Stella Maynard and her friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later adopted Rusty as well. Aunt Jamesina kept house for the girls during their remaining two years at Redmond College, offering them homely wisdom, cheerful company, and motherly care. When the girls graduated and Patty's Place was returned to its owners, Aunt Jamesina chose to remain in Kingsport or return home, taking all three cats with her to Green Gables before heading back.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P56](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0056), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c35 P8](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0008), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008), [v3 c38 P9](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0009)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina because her father James was drowned at sea a month before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Had a daughter named Elizabeth who became an M.A. and went to India as a foreign missionary  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Had numerous suitors in her youth, whom she often laughed at  <sub>[v3 c35 P23](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0023), [v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> The teens are such a nice part of life. I’m glad I’ve never gone out of them myself.  <sub>[v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> When you’ve learned to laugh at the things that should be laughed at, and not to laugh at those that shouldn’t, you’ve got wisdom and understanding.  <sub>[v3 c37 P20](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0020)</sub>

> You can’t learn it in a college course. You’ve been to college four years and I never was, but I know heaps more than you do, young ladies.  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>
